title: New Study Shows Unequal Access to Breast Cancer Screening in England
subtitle: Research reveals that minority ethnic groups and people with learning disabilities face significant barriers to early diagnosis.

summary.en: A new study from the University of Surrey highlights major differences in how breast cancer is diagnosed in England. People from minority ethnic backgrounds are much less likely to be diagnosed through routine screening programs. Instead, these individuals are often diagnosed through emergency care, which can lead to worse health outcomes. The research also found that people with learning disabilities face longer wait times for both diagnosis and treatment. Experts are now calling for better policies to ensure that everyone has equal access to life-saving cancer care.
summary.zh: 薩里大學的一項新研究凸顯了英格蘭在乳癌診斷上的重大差異。少數族裔透過常規篩檢計畫被診斷出罹癌的可能性遠低於一般人，他們往往需透過緊急醫療服務才被診斷出來，這可能導致較差的健康預後。研究亦發現，身心障礙者在診斷與治療上皆面臨更長的等待時間。專家目前正呼籲制定更好的政策，以確保所有人都能平等地獲得救命的癌症照護。

paragraphs.en: A significant new study has highlighted that people from minority ethnic backgrounds in England are facing serious challenges when it comes to breast cancer diagnosis. The research, conducted by academics at the University of Surrey and supported by the charity Breast Cancer Now, shows that these individuals are up to 33% less likely to be diagnosed through routine screening programs. Instead, they are more likely to be diagnosed only when they arrive at a hospital in an emergency.
paragraphs.zh: 一項重大的新研究指出，英格蘭的少數族裔在乳癌診斷方面面臨嚴峻挑戰。這項由薩里大學 (University of Surrey) 學者進行、並獲得慈善機構「乳癌現在」(Breast Cancer Now) 支持的研究顯示，這些族群透過常規篩檢計畫被診斷出罹癌的可能性降低了高達 33%。相反地，他們往往要等到病情嚴重而緊急就醫時，才被診斷出患病。

paragraphs.en: Routine screening is a vital health service where doctors check people for signs of cancer before they show any symptoms. Finding cancer early is very important because it allows for faster treatment and better chances of recovery. Breast cancer is the most common cancer in women globally, and it is a leading cause of death for women under the age of 50. Because of this, identifying women at high risk as early as possible is a major priority for health officials.
paragraphs.zh: 常規篩檢是一項至關重要的醫療服務，醫師會藉此在患者出現任何症狀前檢查是否有罹癌跡象。早期發現癌症非常重要，因為這能讓患者及早接受治療，並提高康復機率。乳癌是全球女性最常見的癌症，也是 50 歲以下女性的主要死因。因此，盡早識別高風險女性是衛生官員的首要任務。

paragraphs.en: The study looked at data from over 86,000 adults diagnosed with the disease between 2009 and 2019. The results showed that people from Black, Asian, and mixed ethnic backgrounds, as well as those from poorer areas, were significantly less likely to benefit from early screening. Furthermore, these same groups were up to 37% more likely to be diagnosed through an emergency presentation—a situation where a patient goes to the hospital because their condition has already become very serious.
paragraphs.zh: 該研究分析了 2009 年至 2019 年間超過 8 萬 6 千名確診患者的數據。結果顯示，非裔、亞裔、混血族群以及居住在較貧困地區的民眾，從早期篩檢中獲益的可能性顯著較低。此外，這些族群透過緊急就醫被診斷出罹癌的可能性高出 37%，這種情況是指患者因病情已變得非常嚴重而被迫前往醫院。

paragraphs.en: Manveet Basra, an associate director at Breast Cancer Now, stated that these findings show that people from marginalized groups face inequalities at every stage of their experience with breast cancer. She noted that these differences tragically impact survival rates. According to Basra, understanding these barriers is the first step toward removing them. The charity is now working with policymakers to improve access to screening and to ensure that health campaigns meet the needs of all people, regardless of their background.
paragraphs.zh: 「乳癌現在」的副主任曼維特·巴斯拉 (Manveet Basra) 表示，這些發現顯示邊緣化族群在乳癌治療的每個階段都面臨不平等。她指出，這些差異對存活率造成了令人遺憾的影響。巴斯拉認為，了解這些障礙是消除它們的第一步。該慈善機構目前正與政策制定者合作，以改善篩檢管道，並確保健康宣導活動能滿足所有人的需求，無論其背景為何。

paragraphs.en: The research also examined the experiences of people living with learning disabilities. The findings were concerning: these individuals faced an 18% longer wait time to receive a diagnosis compared to those without such disabilities. Additionally, they experienced a 10% longer wait time before starting their treatment. These delays can make a massive difference in how well a patient recovers from the disease.
paragraphs.zh: 這項研究也檢視了身心障礙者的就醫經驗。結果令人擔憂：與沒有身心障礙的患者相比，這些人在獲得診斷前需等待的時間長了 18%。此外，他們在開始治療前的等待時間也多了 10%。這些延誤可能會對患者的康復成效產生巨大影響。

paragraphs.en: This new study adds to a growing body of evidence showing that health outcomes are not equal for everyone in England. Previous research has already pointed to similar problems. For example, an analysis by QualityWatch, which is a program from the Nuffield Trust and the Health Foundation, looked at patient experiences in 2022. It found that while one in five people across England need to visit their general practitioner (GP)—a local family doctor—three or more times before getting a cancer diagnosis, this number jumps to one in three for people from ethnic minority backgrounds.
paragraphs.zh: 這項新研究增添了越來越多的證據，顯示英格蘭的醫療成果並非人人平等。先前的研究也曾指出類似問題。例如，由納菲爾德信託基金 (Nuffield Trust) 與健康基金會 (Health Foundation) 共同推動的「品質觀察」(QualityWatch) 計畫，曾針對 2022 年的患者經驗進行分析。研究發現，雖然全英格蘭平均每五人中就有一人需要看診三次或以上才能獲得癌症診斷，但對於少數族裔背景的民眾來說，這個比例卻高達每三人中就有一人。

paragraphs.en: Furthermore, research from the UK Health Security Agency has suggested that young Black women are more likely to develop aggressive breast cancer tumors. Despite this, these women are often under-represented in clinical research, meaning that scientists may not have enough information to provide the best possible care for them. Dr. Rob Kerrison, the lead investigator of the University of Surrey study, explained that while it has been known for some time that some groups of women have poorer survival rates than others, this new data provides a clearer picture of why these gaps exist.
paragraphs.zh: 此外，英國衛生安全局 (UK Health Security Agency) 的研究顯示，年輕非裔女性罹患侵襲性乳癌腫瘤的機率較高。儘管如此，這些女性在臨床研究中的代表性往往不足，這意味著科學家可能缺乏足夠的資訊來為她們提供最佳照護。薩里大學研究計畫主持人羅伯·克里森博士 (Dr. Rob Kerrison) 解釋，雖然學界早已知曉某些女性族群的存活率較低，但這項新數據更清楚地呈現了這些差距存在的原因。

paragraphs.en: Moving forward, the goal is to create a more equal healthcare system. Experts emphasize that the current situation is unacceptable and requires urgent action. By identifying the specific reasons why certain groups are missing out on early screening, health organizations hope to design better services. This includes improving public awareness, making sure that information is easy to understand for everyone, and providing support services that address the diverse needs of the population. Ensuring that every woman has an equal chance to catch cancer early is essential for improving survival rates across the country.
paragraphs.zh: 展望未來，目標是建立一個更平等的醫療體系。專家強調，目前的狀況令人無法接受，必須採取緊急行動。透過釐清特定族群錯過早期篩檢的具體原因，醫療機構希望能設計出更好的服務。這包括提升公眾意識、確保資訊對所有人而言都易於理解，以及提供能解決多元人口需求的支援服務。確保每位女性都有平等的機會及早發現癌症，對於提升全國的存活率至關重要。

quiz.question: According to the study, how much more likely are people from minority ethnic backgrounds to be diagnosed through an emergency presentation compared to others?
quiz.explanationZh: 正確答案為 C。根據文章第三段，研究顯示少數族裔群體透過緊急就醫（emergency presentation）被診斷出乳癌的可能性高出 37%。選項 A（18%）是學習障礙患者診斷延遲的數據；選項 B（33%）是這些群體較少透過常規篩檢被診斷出的比例；選項 D（10%）則是學習障礙患者治療延遲的比例。考生需仔細區分文中不同的百分比數據。

quiz.question: What can be inferred about the relationship between clinical research and the care provided to young Black women?

options.A: Clinical research is currently focusing exclusively on the needs of young Black women.
options.B: The lack of diverse representation in research limits the effectiveness of medical treatments for these women.
options.C: Aggressive breast cancer tumors in young Black women are caused by a lack of access to GP services.
options.D: Scientists have already gathered enough data to fully understand why these women have lower survival rates.

quiz.explanationZh: 正確答案為 B。根據第七段，文中提到年輕黑人女性在臨床研究中常被「低估（under-represented）」，導致科學家缺乏足夠資訊來提供最佳照護。這暗示了研究代表性不足直接影響了醫療決策的品質。選項 A 與文意相反；選項 C 將腫瘤成因與 GP 服務混為一談，文中並未證實此因果關係；選項 D 錯誤，因為文章明確指出研究仍需更多資訊來填補知識缺口。

quiz.question: In the fourth paragraph, what does the word 'marginalized' mean as it is used in the context of the article?

options.A: Groups that are treated as insignificant or pushed to the edge of society.
options.B: People who live in rural areas far away from major city hospitals.
options.C: Individuals who have recently moved to England from another country.
options.D: Patients who have been diagnosed with a terminal illness.

quiz.explanationZh: 正確答案為 A。在第四段中，Manveet Basra 使用「marginalized groups」來形容面臨醫療不平等的族群。Marginalized 指的是被邊緣化、在社會中缺乏權力或資源的群體。選項 B 僅指地理位置，過於狹隘；選項 C 指的是移民，但文章涵蓋範圍更廣；選項 D 指的是病情，與社會地位無關。從前後文討論「不平等（inequalities）」來看，A 是最精確的描述。

quiz.question: What is the primary message of the article regarding breast cancer diagnosis in England?

options.A: Routine screening programs are being replaced by emergency hospital visits for all patients.
options.B: The UK government has successfully solved the issue of health inequality for minority groups.
options.C: There are significant, systemic inequalities in breast cancer diagnosis that require urgent policy changes.
options.D: Learning disabilities are the only factor causing delays in cancer treatment in the UK healthcare system.

quiz.explanationZh: 正確答案為 C。文章的核心在於探討少數族裔、貧困地區民眾及身心障礙者在乳癌診斷上所面臨的系統性障礙，並強調這是不公平且需迫切改善的議題。選項 A 錯誤，因為篩檢仍是重要服務；選項 B 與文意完全相反，問題尚未解決；選項 D 錯誤，因為文章同時討論了種族與經濟因素，並非僅限於學習障礙。
